m:
Constitutional AI Prompting introduces a structured governance layer into prompt design. Instead of relying solely on implicit alignment from training, the system injects an explicit list of principles that the model must use to evaluate and revise its responses.

Core Pipeline:

1. Constitution Definition
A list of guiding principles is provided. These can include:

• safety rules
• ethical constraints
• legal compliance
• factual integrity
• user respect

Example principle:
"The AI should avoid generating advice that could cause physical harm."

2. Initial Response Generation
The model produces a normal answer to the user query.

3. Constitutional Critique
The model reviews its own answer against each principle in the constitution and identifies violations.

4. Self-Revision
The model rewrites the answer to comply with the principles.

5. Final Output
The revised answer is returned.

Advanced Deployment Patterns (2024–2026):

• hierarchical constitutions
• domain-specific constitutions
• policy-driven governance prompts
• automated compliance scoring
• safety audit traces

This approach creates a transparent alignment mechanism where the reasoning for safety decisions can be traced to explicit rules.
